notesRecorded.location: Authority section — 'D-054 does not apply. This is Route C, not Route B.'
notesRecorded.observation: The entry excludes D-054 by name but says nothing about D-057, whose operative sentence opens with a general phrase: 'Later preview-scope owner-recording entries must satisfy the preconditions and pins in the adopted turn-3 subject.' D-068 self-describes as an owner-recording entry in preview scope, so on a first reading of that sentence alone a reader may take D-057 to reach it — and D-068 satisfies none of D-057's preconditions.
notesRecorded.whyItIsNotAFinding: D-057 genuinely does not govern this entry, and I verified that three independent ways rather than inferring it. Its decision-type line states 'Mechanics only. Authority is user-made D-054, not this entry', so excluding D-054 excludes D-057 with it. Its preconditions require 'live D-054 / D-057 / row Route B selection' and its pin list requires the D-054 user-amendment path, Route B IDs and commits, and a Route A remainder — a set that is unsatisfiable by construction for a Route C row, which is itself evidence it was never meant to reach one. And its own reversibility clause scopes it to 'every owner recording that cites D-054/D-057', which D-068 does not do. The entry's conclusion is correct.
notesRecorded.whyItIsWorthRecording: The resolution is clean but the reader has to go and find it, and D-057's operative sentence is broad on its face. One clause — that D-057's mechanics govern the D-054 grant and lapse with it — would close the question in the entry itself, in the same way the D-054 exclusion already does.

summary: Subject and prompt held at their dispatched digests, both read-only. The whole risk on this entry is the authority, because it is an owner recording that deliberately does not use the owner-recording grant the rest of this family runs on — and it gets that right. D-054's own text is decisive: it says 'D-000 already delegated coordinator and product-authority decisions' and that D-054 was needed only for the additional V1 owner roles, which it enumerates as Evidence, TM, D9, retention, R-1 and identity surfaces. The product owner is not among them, DR-010 is Route C, and D-054's grant is expressly for 'preview Route B dispositions'. So D-000 is the correct authority and D-054 is correctly disclaimed. All five cited digests match live bytes, the D-066 commit resolves and is confirmed as D-066's first COORD appearance, and the entry's characterisation of the candidate is accurate against the candidate's own fields.
whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: 469274041da731de484eb2e2c118939f69c2488242778843b39e407fd09d293d, three measurements at start and again at end, equal to the dispatched frozen digest, -r--r--r-- at both ends. Prompt held at 8047515f8b2995c76a56f0221824053a6ad87914278aa92940a8d293cda58fc7, also read-only.

The attack 'treats D-054 as the authority' fails, and the entry is right on the merits rather than merely disclaiming. D-054's own text reads 'D-000 already delegated coordinator and product-authority decisions. Completing condition 1's alternative limb also requires the named V1 owners (Evidence, TM, D9, retention, R-1, identity surfaces) to record accepted preview Route B dispositions.' That sentence does two things at once: it confirms D-000 already covers product-authority decisions, and it limits D-054 to the named V1 roles and to Route B. The product owner is not in that list and DR-010 is Route C, so D-054 is inapplicable exactly as the entry states, and D-000 supplies the authority.

D-000's grant covers this act and I read its full terms rather than the one clause the entry quotes. Its decision is 'The assistant completes the coop design end-to-end, making coordinator/product-authority decisions on the user's behalf', and file 08's DR-010 owner cell is 'Product owner'. There is no carve-out excluding owner recordings. Clause 1 requires that any decision which would have needed the user go to adversarial review, which is this cycle; clause 3 requires the decision, alternatives, rationale, reviewer verdict with digest, reversibility class and overturn procedure, all of which the entry carries; clause 5 requires PREFERENCE-LADEN marking, which is present.

D-000 clause 5's specific requirement — that a PREFERENCE-LADEN decision's overturn 'is written to cost less than the decision did' — is satisfied. The decision took two candidate versions, two independent review rounds and a separately committed coordinator recording. The overturn is 'Compound. Overturn: C-D068, plus reconciliation of any later MF-6 note. Does not overturn D-066', which leaves the accepted candidate and its recording standing and so is plainly cheaper than what it undoes.

The route classification is correct at source: COORD's routing line reads 'DR-010 route C PREFERENCE-LADEN (P-1/P-2/G3 successor, jointly with DR-117 and R16)', matching the entry's decision type, its Route C claim, and its treatment of DR-117 and R16 as joint-but-separate.

The attack 'silent SATISFIED' fails. The header states 'Does not mark SATISFIED', clause 2 scopes any effect to 'condition 1 for DR-010 within architecture-preview scope only', clause 3 states 'Does not mark DR-010 SATISFIED', and the readiness effect reads 'Zero SATISFIED. Conditions 2–5 unchanged.'

The attack 'closes DR-117 / R16' fails three times: the header states 'Does not close DR-117 or DR-011-R16', clause 3 repeats it, and the alternatives section rejects it by name — 'Also close DR-117 / R16 here. Rejected: independently required; would bundle.'

The predicate claim about D-066 is true. D-066 is present in COORD and ADOPTED, its cited commit c2d7f7704be9e89dac8859f15e086b3694c3227b resolves to 'D-066: record product-boundary-preview.v2 as DR-010 candidate', and a git log -S search confirms that commit is D-066's first COORD appearance. D-066's adopted text states 'Condition 1 does not discharge until the product owner records', so this entry is accurately described as 'the later owner act D-066 left owed'.

All five cited digests match live bytes: COORD 281bd81d…, file 08 6547e6ac…, the candidate at ff7a0913…, my own verdict at d5c1eccd… and the Codex verdict at 8b64732c…. The candidate digest is the same value I measured at both ends of my v2 review, so the artifact being recorded is byte-identical to the one I reviewed, and the recital of my verdict as 'ACCEPT 0/0' is exact — that file is the one I wrote and it records ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 advisories.

The entry's characterisation of the candidate is accurate against the candidate's own fields: its seven previewDisposition values are six exclusions and one NOT REPLACED, matching 'PB-1..PB-6 EXCLUDED, PB-7 NOT REPLACED'; preservedV1Decisions carries P-1, P-2 and G3-SUBSTRATE; and CD-RT-5 is untouched, which is also consistent with file 08, where CD-RT-5 belongs to the DR-001 and DR-008 pins rather than DR-010's.

The attacks 'condition 5 / docs/v2/implementation' and 'file 08 edited' fail: the header refuses to authorize docs/v2/implementation/, clause 3 preserves condition 5 as the only implementation authorization, clause 4 refuses the file 08 edit under MF-6 and defers a cell note as a separate act, file 08 measures unchanged at its cited digest, and git reports zero modified tracked files.

Examined and cleared: the entry carries no Route A remainder section, unlike the D-060, D-061 and D-065 owner recordings. That is correct rather than an omission — a Route A remainder is what a Route B election leaves owed, and this is a Route C recording. Requiring one here would import a Route B concept into a row that has no Route B selection.

Examined and cleared: the entry carries no 'Operative riders' line. None is needed, because both independent reviews of the candidate are clean ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 advisories, so there is no advisory to classify as operative or non-operative — unlike D-060, which required that clause because one reviewer returned ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES.

Examined and cleared: the alternative 'Wait for a human product-owner act. Rejected: D-000 already delegates product-authority decisions.' I checked whether the corpus anywhere reserves product-owner acts to the human. It does not: D-054's limitation runs the other way, resting on the V1 owner roles having 'no other human', and the one place a human product owner is named — DR-008's posture half, owned by sfbreen — was already closed rather than held open pending a human act. The rejection is consistent with the corpus.

consentNote: I CONSENT with zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX. This entry does the thing the family has been carefully avoiding — recording an owner disposition without D-054 — and it is right to, because D-054 was never the authority for a Route C product row. I did not take that on the entry's word: D-054's own text says D-000 already delegated product-authority decisions and limits itself to the named V1 owner roles recording preview Route B dispositions, and the product owner is in neither set. The two structural absences a reader might flag, a Route A remainder and an operative-riders line, are both correct for this instrument rather than omissions. My one note is that the entry disclaims D-054 explicitly but leaves D-057's broad-sounding opening sentence to the reader; D-057 does not reach this entry, and I verified that from its authority line, its unsatisfiable preconditions and its own reversibility scoping.
